title: An Undo toast for changes that are easy to make by mistake
subtitle: Mock-ups for #1804 on Simple's Roadmap with the real feature panel; every Undo in the frames really takes the change back in the mock app

decisions.name: The toast
decisions.question: Where does the Undo toast sit, how long does it stay, and what happens when several changes come fast?
decisions.common: Every proposal says the change in a few words with an Undo button, is read out politely by a screen reader (it never takes the focus), holds while hovered or focused, and is fed by the real changes: the frames remove a real dependency and move a real feature on Simple's Roadmap, and Undo really puts them back. Today one toast shows for 10 seconds and a new change replaces it, so an earlier Undo is lost. The working draft banner's own button, 'Undo my last change', is a different tool: it takes back your newest change in the draft at any time, toast or not, while a toast's Undo takes back the one change it names, while it shows.

proposals.name: Newest wins
proposals.what: Today's single toast in the bottom-right corner, shortened to 8 seconds with a thin bar that shows the time left, and Ctrl Z beside Undo. A new change replaces the toast; Ctrl Z still undoes the newest change while its toast is up.
proposals.plus: Smallest change from today; never covers more than one line of the page.
proposals.cost: Undo the newest change: 1 click or Ctrl Z (today 1 click). Undo a change made one step earlier: not here; redo it by hand, 2 to 5 steps (today the same).

proposals.name: Stack of three
proposals.what: Each change gets its own toast in the bottom-right corner, newest at the bottom, each with its own Undo and its own 8-second bar. At most three show; older ones fold into a '2 more' button that opens them. An undone change leaves the stack; the banner's count drops.
proposals.plus: Every recent change is one click away without opening anything.
proposals.cost: Undo any of the last three: 1 click. Undo a fourth or older: 2 clicks (N more, Undo). Covers up to three toasts' height of the page's corner.

proposals.name: One toast that counts
proposals.what: One toast in the bottom-right corner shows the newest change with Undo and Ctrl Z. Changes made while it is up fold into a line under it, '2 earlier changes', that opens a list with an Undo for each. 8 seconds, restarted by each new change. Undo in the open list closes it again.
proposals.why: It keeps today's single toast and place, so the page is never covered by a stack, yet no change made in a fast run is lost: each stays one or two clicks away until the toast closes, and the item's history after that (UT3).
proposals.plus: Ctrl Z and the screen reader both reach the newest change first; one line of height at rest.
proposals.cost: Undo the newest: 1 click or Ctrl Z. Undo an earlier one: 2 clicks (earlier changes, Undo). Today: an earlier one is lost.

proposals.name: Strip under the title
proposals.what: No floating toast: a strip under the title and the view switch shows the newest change, how many changes were made on this page, and Undo. It has no timer and stays until the person leaves the page or closes it.
proposals.plus: Never runs out while a person reads; never covers the chart's lower edge.
proposals.cost: Undo the newest: 1 click, any time while on the page. Undo an earlier one: not here; the item's history. Pushes the page down one row while it stays.

decisions.name: Which changes get one
decisions.question: Which changes get an Undo toast, and what does Undo mean for a commenter's proposal?
decisions.common: Owners and approvers change Simple at once; a commenter's change becomes a proposal that waits in Needs a decision, as today. Deleting a PRD keeps its confirm in every proposal. The frames make real changes in the feature panel of F-79 Weekly alert digest: its status, then Cut from its menu, then a commenter's status change. While a cut's toast shows, the panel's 'Cut on … by …' bar waits, so one Undo shows; when the toast is gone, that bar's Restore brings it back.

proposals.name: Every change, Withdraw
proposals.what: Every direct change gets the toast with Undo: a status, dates, a drag in the priority order, removing a dependency or a link, cutting, moving to Trash and a bulk change (one toast for the whole batch). Cutting drops its confirm in favour of Undo. A commenter's proposal gets the same toast with Withdraw, which takes the proposal back before anyone decides.
proposals.why: One rule a person can learn: whatever you just did, the toast can take it back. It removes the cut's confirm step, and a commenter gets a matching way back that says what really happens to a proposal (it is withdrawn, as Removed already does for a restore).
proposals.plus: Matches the Withdraw that Removed already offers for a proposed restore.
proposals.cost: Cut: 1 click (today 2: Cut, then confirm). Undo it: 1 more. A commenter takes back a proposal: 1 click (today: Needs a decision, find it, withdraw, about 3).

proposals.name: Only the hard to redo
proposals.what: Only changes that are hard to redo get the toast: removing a dependency or a link, cutting, moving to Trash and a bulk change. A status, dates or a drag in the order show a small Saved tick beside the field instead; they are put back by changing them again or from the item's history. A commenter's change gets the same mark, 'Proposed', with Withdraw in it.
proposals.plus: Fewer toasts on a busy page; quick edits stay quiet.
proposals.cost: Undo a status change: 2 clicks (Change, pick the old one) and the person must remember it. Cut: 1 click, Undo 1.

proposals.name: Confirm the big ones
proposals.what: Small changes (status, dates, order) get the toast with Undo; cutting, moving to Trash and bulk changes keep a confirm step and get no Undo. A commenter's proposal gets a plain toast that names Proposals on it, where Withdraw is.
proposals.plus: A person reads what a big change will do before it happens.
proposals.cost: Cut: 2 clicks, as today, and no Undo; taking it back: Removed, Restore (2 clicks).

decisions.name: After the toast
decisions.question: Once the toast is gone, where does a person still undo a change?
decisions.common: Each Undo puts the old state back through the API and writes one history line. The frames cut F-79 Weekly alert digest from its panel, let the toast run out, then take the cut back. Today the only way back after the toast is Removed (for a cut) and Trash (for a delete); the working draft banner's 'Undo my last change' takes back only your newest change.

proposals.name: History in the panel
proposals.what: The feature panel, the one every page opens, gets a History section right under its status line: each change to the feature, newest first, who made it and when, with Undo on each. A commenter sees Propose undo instead. On a phone it sits in the panel sheet as a closed section. For a cut, History's Undo replaces the Restore in the panel's 'Cut on … by …' line, so one cut has one Undo.
proposals.why: It lives where the feature already is on every page (Roadmap, Goal map, Priorities, Home), covers changes by anyone and not only this visit, and needs no new page or button in the app's frame.
proposals.plus: Shows who changed what, so a person can see why something moved before taking it back.
proposals.cost: Open the feature (1), History (1), Undo (1): 3 clicks, any time. Today: redo by hand, or Removed for a cut (2). Detailed gets no History of its own: a Detailed person switches to Simple (the Simple and Detailed switch in the side bar) and opens the feature there, one more click; the owner to agree.

proposals.name: Your changes list
proposals.what: A 'Your changes' button under the rail's pages opens today's changes made by this person on any page, newest first, each with Undo. On a phone it is a round clock button above the tab bar.
proposals.plus: One place for everything a person did today, across pages.
proposals.cost: Your changes (1), Undo (1): 2 clicks, today only and only one's own changes.

proposals.name: Removed and Trash only
proposals.what: Nothing new after the toast: a cut comes back from Removed, a delete from Trash, as today; a status, dates or a link are changed back by hand.
proposals.cost: A cut: Removed (1), Restore (1) = 2 clicks. A status or dates change: redo by hand and remember the old value.
